title: Probing Structural Origins of Ambient Pressure Superconductivity and Charge Modulation in Nickelate Thin Films with Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Nickelates are known for having rich phase diagrams with strongly correlated quantum phases and phenomena such as metal-to-insulator transition (MIT), charge order (CO) and high-temperature superconductivity (HT SC) [1-4]. Despite considerable efforts, the interplay of structural modifications and electronic configuration for many of these phases is not fully understood. This is especially complicated by the presence of disorder and secondary phases which make detecting subtle structural changes challenging across phase transitions [5, 6]. Hence, a local probe that can disentangle disorder and secondary phases from the pristine structure at atomic resolution is required to correlate electronic and atomic behavior. Although conventional STEM techniques such as annular bright field (ABF) and integrated differential phase contrast (iDPC) are commonly used for atomic-resolution characterization, they suffer from artifacts confounding precise measurement of atomic positions, especially of light elements such as oxygen [7, 8]. A recently implemented STEM technique, multislice electron ptychography (MEP), allows for quantitative measurements of light and heavy atoms at the highest possible lateral resolution with added depth information, while avoiding many of the artifacts associated with the other techniques [9]. Here, we use MEP to resolve the structure of two different nickelate systems: Nd-based infinite layer nickelates (NdNiO2) and La-based bi-layer nickelates (La3Ni2O7).
